channel.title: Architecture of sites and areas
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Architecture of sites and areas" - What do you imagine the architecture of sites and areas owned by the SCP foundation to be like?

item.title: Re: Architecture of sites and areas
item.content:encoded: I'd go for Soviet Modular Designed, with specific modules for specific endevours (sturdier for Containment), each Site would have it's genius locii though, Site-38 is a backwater storage place with probably a 70s old feel, while other sites devoted to research must look white and crisp.

item.title: Re: Architecture of sites and areas
item.content:encoded:
I view the office area of Foundation sites much the same as a typical high-security national lab or defense contractor. High security, but otherwise pretty normal.

So basically, strict keycard + biometric access, some discreet armed security guards, a ban on outside electronics, but plenty of nicknacks and personal decorations, motivational posters, decent snacks and coffee, a couple of vending machines, some plants (probably fake), a mix of cubicles and personal offices, conference rooms, and cake on the break room table for birthdays (possibly some gluten free cookies as well).

item.title: Re: Architecture of sites and areas
item.content:encoded:
I would actually find an in-between more plausible, with zones containing dangerous items or SCPs to be built rigid over anything else, and with sectors where regular staff spend most of their time designed to improve morale

This sums up my headcanon pretty well. I like to think that Foundation personnel are allowed to have personal decorations and whatnot so long as they're not overly intrusive (the Kiryu Labs Hub tales mention small snippets of this sort of thing, like a seahorse paperweight, potted plants, and a lizard terrarium in a break room).

item.title: Re: Architecture of sites and areas
Architecture of sites and areas
item.content:encoded:
What do you imagine the architecture of sites and areas owned by the SCP foundation to be like? Would they promote the morale of foundation personnel by prioritizing the design, or would they much rather prefer typical modular designs, such as how the Soviets used to rapidly build housing using prefabricated parts.

I would actually find an in-between more plausible, with zones containing dangerous items or SCPs to be built rigid over anything else, and with sectors where regular staff spend most of their time designed to improve morale, either by using less 'depressive' materials such as plain concrete and moving where they can to glass or wood, adding plant life and regular furniture found in any office space. (Maybe even leisure spaces?)

From what I've read so far I'm pretty sure the foundation cares a lot about the morale of it's staff, especially with all the precautions taken on SCP-035's mental effects.

What do you think?
